scenario: [LEXP.3.8] scalar min/max over two Ints, which [LDET.3.2.2] makes exact 64-bit values. 2^53+1 and 2^53 are distinct Ints and round to the same double, so a min/max that compares through double returns the wrong operand for one argument order. The guard `min(t.x, t.y) == t.y and max(t.y, t.x) == t.x` with x = 2^53+1, y = 2^53 holds only for an exact compare: through double, min returns its first argument x and max its first argument y. Path: builtins.c builtin_min / builtin_max (DS_FN_MIN / DS_FN_MAX); Mercury ds.eval pick. fact_count 2 = T plus the Hit the rule emits.
rules_ds:
schema T scope logical:
    x: Int key
    y: Int key

schema Hit scope logical:
    d: Int key

rule r:
    T t where min(t.x, t.y) == t.y and max(t.y, t.x) == t.x
->
    emit Hit logical d: 0
